---
title: "Glen Canyon Dam"
---

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all()
library(tidyverse)
```

Daily discharge, Colorado River, USGS NWIS (`dataRetrieval::readNWISdv`, parameter `00060`, 1950–2025):

- `cisco_cfs`: near Cisco, UT (`09180500`) — upstream of Glen Canyon Dam, natural flow.
- `leesferry_cfs`: at Lees Ferry, AZ (`09380000`) — immediately downstream of the dam.

Dam closure: **1963-03-13**. Before: Lees Ferry ≈ translated copy of Cisco. After: Lake Powell decouples the two — releases follow hydropower demand, not upstream timing. Known date, known mechanism, known direction of effect.

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| label: gcd-load

cisco <- read_csv("../data/real-data/glen-canyon-dam/cisco-daily.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))
leesferry <- read_csv("../data/real-data/glen-canyon-dam/leesferry-daily.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))

dam_closure <- as.Date("1963-03-13")

X_monthly <- inner_join(cisco, leesferry, by = "Date") |>
  mutate(year = year(Date), month = month(Date)) |>
  group_by(year, month) |>
  summarize(cisco_cfs = mean(cisco_cfs), leesferry_cfs = mean(leesferry_cfs), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", year, month)),
         regime = if_else(date < dam_closure, "pre", "post")) |>
  arrange(date)
```

## Deseasonalizing

Raw series carry a strong annual cycle (snowmelt pulse). The cycle's *shape* changes at the dam — sharp pre-dam, damped post-dam — so one climatology for the whole record is wrong. Fit calendar-month means separately within each regime, subtract.

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: gcd-deseasonalize

clim <- X_monthly |>
  group_by(regime, month) |>
  summarize(cisco_clim = mean(cisco_cfs), lf_clim = mean(leesferry_cfs), .groups = "drop")

X_resid <- X_monthly |>
  left_join(clim, by = c("regime", "month")) |>
  mutate(cisco_resid = cisco_cfs - cisco_clim,
         lf_resid = leesferry_cfs - lf_clim)

downsample <- function(df, k) df[seq(1, nrow(df), by = k), ]
X_ds3 <- downsample(X_resid, 3)
X_ds6 <- downsample(X_resid, 6)

win <- 25
```

## Full Record

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Residuals

```{R fig-gcd-residual}
#| echo: false

X_resid |>
  select(date, cisco_resid, lf_resid) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, color = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = dam_closure, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Deseasonalized Residuals", x = NULL, y = "Discharge anomaly (cfs)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Change point is obvious: Lees Ferry residual amplitude collapses after 1963 — the dam damps variance, not just level.

## ACF

```{R acf-gcd-full}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(2, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))
acf(X_resid$cisco_resid, main = "", xlab = "", ylab = "cisco_resid")
acf(X_resid$lf_resid, main = "", xlab = "", ylab = "lf_resid")
mtext("Lag (months)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 0.5)
```

Not handled. Lag-1: 0.71 (`cisco_resid`), 0.75 (`lf_resid`) — real hydrologic memory, not a seasonality artifact.

## Trend

```{R trend-gcd-full}

X_mat <- as.matrix(X_resid[, c("cisco_resid", "lf_resid")])
plot_ece_terms(X_mat, window = win)
```

## ACF

```{R acf-gcd-ds6}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(2, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

```

Lag-1 drops to 0.11 / 0.27. Cisco effectively white; Lees Ferry keeps some dependence (deliberate flow-smoothing at the dam). `k = 12` was tried and reverses this (lag-1 back to 0.64 / 0.50 — annual drought/wet-cycle persistence, a different dependence structure downsampling-by-calendar-position can't fix). `k = 6` is the working choice.

## Naive vs. Oracle vs. ECE

- **Naive**: Pearson correlation, full residual series, ignoring the change point.
- **Oracle**: Pearson correlation within each known regime (uses the change-point date).
- **ECE**: `ece.cor()`, blind to the change-point date, given only a minimum segment length `L = 4`.

```{R gcd-naive-oracle-ece}
#| echo: false

report <- function(df, L = 4) {
  pre <- filter(df, regime == "pre")
  post <- filter(df, regime == "post")
  tibble(
    n = nrow(df),
    naive = cor(df$cisco_resid, df$lf_resid),
    oracle_pre = cor(pre$cisco_resid, pre$lf_resid),
    oracle_post = cor(post$cisco_resid, post$lf_resid),
    ece = ece.cor(df$cisco_resid, df$lf_resid, L = L)
  )
}

bind_rows(
  Full = report(X_resid),
  `k = 3` = report(X_ds3),
  `k = 6` = report(X_ds6),
  .id = "transform"
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

At `L = 2` (not shown), ECE on the full (undownsampled) residual series returns a correlation estimate outside $[-1,1]$ — the uncorrected residual autocorrelation breaks the estimator outright, not just its efficiency. At `L = 4` it stays in range but far from both Naive and Oracle. As `k` grows and residual autocorrelation drops, ECE's estimate rises toward Naive's. Neither Naive nor ECE recovers Oracle's two different regime correlations (0.99 pre, ~0.59 post) — both assume one shared correlation, which the data doesn't actually have. That's a real limitation, not downsampling's fault: it needs a model with a change point in $\Sigma$, not just $\theta$.
